newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Pharmaceuticals, Danubius push BUX index higher.
newsitem.headline: Pharmaceuticals, Danubius push BUX index higher.

text.p: Losers outnumbered gainers on the Budapest Stock Exchange on Thursday despite the fact that the market turned bullish after a weaker opening, traders said.
The BUX index ended at 3,517.51 points, up 24.02, propelled mainly by the pharmaceutical sector and hotelier Danubius.
BUX index futures rose for the three nearest and the longest maturities by 20.00 to 45.00 points, they firmed a shade 0.50 points for June 1997, were steady for December 1997.
Traders said the market's daily picture was a result of different opinions of different groups of investors.
"(Domestic) small investors and speculators say that the shares are overvalued, while the institutional and foreign investors have different opinion," said Tamas Revesz of Gog Securities.
Traders said they saw signs that pharmaceutical Egis is about to take over the trend-setter role from oil company MOL.
Egis shares which Revesz said "foreigners buy like sugar at 11,000 forints," firmed to a new high of 11,100 forints, although retreated to end at 11,095, up 595.
The other pharmaceuticals maker Richter also strengthened to a daily peak of 9,000 forints, but this time it was not strong enough to hit a new high.
Meanwhile, the market's third drugs share, Human also hit a new high of 2,180 forints, but it came down to end at 2,155, up 105.
Heavy-weight hotelier Danubius ended at 2,860 forints, up 90.
